findings.requirement: Lining must remain on its intended side of the covering with deliberate spacing.
findings.observed: At 60°, the 0.7 mm world-X shift projects from -0.694 to +0.561 mm onto the spine normal. Triangle crossing counts are 1788 / 4050 / 3104 at 0 / 60 / 130°.
findings.cause: Lining is translated on the world X axis instead of offset in the spine local surface frame.
findings.correction: Construct common layer interfaces from a shared reference surface and normals; define bonded regions and terminations.
findings.acceptanceTest: Check signed separation, thickness and contact regions for every sampled pose.
findings.evidence: wizard-grimoire/book.mjs: spinePoint and liner update; measurements.json pairs/poses
findings.reproduction: wizard-grimoire/book.mjs: spinePoint and liner update; measurements.json pairs/poses

findings.remainingUncertainty: Crossing counts are triangle-pair witnesses, not unique collisions or penetration depth. Some contact may be intended; no explicit lining/cover attachment-region allowance establishes these crossings as valid.

findings.requirement: Support ends must connect to board lacing.
findings.observed: At 130°, cord-end centre distances to front/rear lacing surfaces are 3.745 / 3.610 mm; cord radius is 1.2 mm. Broad-phase boxes are disjoint in tested centre-cord/lacing pairs.
findings.cause: Cords and lacing are authored independently; registry attachment is not physical continuity.
findings.correction: Create a single routed support per station, with board entry, channel, and visible terminal.

findings.measurement: At 130°, cord-end centre distances to front/rear lacing surfaces are 3.745 / 3.610 mm; cord radius is 1.2 mm. Broad-phase boxes are disjoint in tested centre-cord/lacing pairs.

findings.requirement: Surface deformation must agree with an explicit material-coordinate model.
findings.observed: Midline cross-section changes 50.668 → 43.011 mm at 60° (-15.11%); corresponding outer-face area changes 15212 → 12928 mm² (-15.01%).
findings.cause: Authored spine curve is rebuilt from independent cover positions with an added bulge; no strain/paring model.
findings.correction: Define a reference binding and neutral surface; distribute bending and compression by layer, with justified limits.

findings.measurement: Midline cross-section changes 50.668 → 43.011 mm at 60° (-15.11%); corresponding outer-face area changes 15212 → 12928 mm² (-15.01%).
findings.remainingUncertainty: This is geometric distortion, not a calibrated leather stress/strain result. Compression can be physically appropriate; magnitude alone is not proof of failure.

findings.requirement: A lower-spine repair must physically bridge the described region.

findings.cause: Description and actual parent/attachment disagree.
findings.correction: Either relocate the repair across the actual spine with coordinated deformation, or describe it honestly as a cover repair.

findings.measurement: Patch and stitches are children of front-cover and reference its leather face.

findings.measurement: 240 leaf identities and 120 closed return pieces exist; sewing loops are positioned on spinePoint, not verified through actual fold holes.

findings.correction: Expose quality/performance tradeoff if production close must meet 30 fps; never reduce physical construction silently.

findings.cause: Controlled authored kinematics were used for a construction study.

viewpoints.name: Hand bookbinder
viewpoints.text: The first question is not whether the spine looks rounded, but whether the sections can actually be sewn, lined and attached to the boards in the order implied by the assembly. The centre cord does not meet its visible lacing terminal in the sampled closed and fully open states. Separate return pieces can be closed solids and still fail to form a folded sheet with their leaves. Build the gathering, support and board attachment as one construction sequence before embellishing bands.

viewpoints.name: Book conservator
viewpoints.text: A repair should make its location and purpose legible. This patch follows the front board, so it cannot establish a lower-spine repair while the spine flexes independently. The cap and endband need an inspectable relationship: the Met describes a folded layer of pared leather protecting an endband. A rolled-looking strip and repeated torus loops alone do not establish that relationship. Concealed construction needs a labelled section, not an obstructed bookmark.

viewpoints.name: Binding historian / bibliographer
viewpoints.text: Keep the proposed supported tight-back identity distinct from later case-binding and hollow-back interpretations. A visible cavity is not by itself evidence of an intentional hollow. Record what is proposed, what is merely a display proxy, and what construction the cited object actually demonstrates. The old studio already says opening/fabrication are deferred; it should not be condemned for absent animation, but its advertised solid export still needs solid geometry.

viewpoints.name: Mechanical engineer
viewpoints.text: Treat the cords, sewn sections, lining, covering and board attachments as a load path. Geometry that stops short cannot transmit the loads implied by the scene unless another attachment is specified. The 15% arc and area change is a strong modelling warning but cannot be converted into material stress without constitutive properties. Covers supported by pads do not prove the binding is in equilibrium. Gravity and external opening controls must remain explicit.

viewpoints.name: Computational geometry specialist
viewpoints.text: A watertight mesh is only one predicate. Multiple closed shells can overlap or be fully contained; both must be tested independently. Open studio spines make their signed-volume result unsuitable as a physical volume. The new hierarchy tests find surface-crossing witnesses between spine and lining, but do not solve coplanar contact or establish a penetration depth. Pair-level attachment regions are needed before contact can be accepted.

viewpoints.name: Animation / simulation specialist
viewpoints.text: The deterministic cycle result is useful, but it certifies only repeatability for that sequence. A moving binding needs material correspondence and connected roots, not independent shapes rebuilt at each angle. Reversal, a partly turned leaf, spread changes and a closing cover must all reach the same physical assembly. ETH page-block separation is relevant to runtime strategy, not evidence validating this spine.

viewpoints.name: Technical artist / material specialist
viewpoints.text: The reviewed spine preset obscures the assembly behind a cover and cradle. The joint capture largely shows broad surfaces rather than the joint. This is a presentation defect independent of polygon count. Box-based shelf books may be effective scene props at distance but cannot inherit the hero book’s inspection promise. Neutral and grazing comparisons should show actual folds, layer edges and contact shadows before grain or warm light is used to sell age.

viewpoints.name: QA / metrology specialist
viewpoints.text: Tests must be able to fail when the named property is broken. The clay-class assertion is non-discriminating; a metadata thickness assertion does not inspect a solid; a resolving attachment ID does not test contact. The invalid-import test now demonstrates state mutation before failure. Unit-scaled tolerance fixtures pass, but this does not calibrate arbitrary mesh penetration, all coordinate transforms or real leather strain. Keep each limited pass bounded.
